target.title: fix(acp): ACP session startup fails when backend does not advertise thinking config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103802 — Every `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` against backends like OpenCode (which only advertise `mode, model` as supported config options) fails immediately with:

```
AcpRuntimeError: ACP backend "acpx" does not accept config key "thinking".: code=ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL
```

The ACP runtime resolves a thinking default (e.g., `"off"` for non-reasoning provider models) and sends it via `setConfigOption`, which the backend rejects. The caller cannot avoid this — passing no `thinking` in `sessions_spawn` does not prevent the injection, and omitting `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` doesn't either.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two layers of defense, following the precedent of PR #81603 (timeout tolerance):

**Layer 1 — Prevention (runtime-options.ts):** A `shouldEmitThinkingConfigOption` guard in `buildRuntimeConfigOptionPairs`. If the backend advertises `configOptionKeys` and none of the thinking aliases (`thinking`, `effort`, `reasoning_effort`, `thought_level`) are in the list, the thinking pair is never emitted. Follows the exact same pattern as the existing `shouldEmitTimeoutConfigOption` guard.

**Layer 2 — Safety net (manager.runtime-controls.ts):** A catch block in `applyManagerRuntimeControls` that silently skips unsupported thinking config options when `setConfigOption` throws. Error detection is restricted to `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL` error code only — value-validation errors (e.g., `-32602`, `invalid params`) are NOT swallowed, so explicit user-selected values that a backend rejects still fail visibly.

## User Impact

ACP spawns targeting backends with limited config support (mode+model only) succeed instead of failing on init. Backends that support thinking/effort continue to work as before — Layer 1 only suppresses emission when the backend explicitly does not advertise the key, and Layer 2 only catches actual unsupported-control rejections.

## Evidence

- 4 files changed, 161 insertions, 1 deletion (2 source + 2 test)
- Follows the existing `shouldEmitTimeoutConfigOption` / `isUnsupportedOptionalTimeoutConfigRejection` patterns exactly
- **9 new tests** across both test files:
  - `runtime-options.test.ts`: 7 tests for thinking advertisement filtering (omitted when unadvertised, emitted for each alias, emitted when unknown, doesn't affect other keys)
  - `manager.runtime-config.test.ts`: 2 tests for thinking rejection handling (unsupported control silently skipped, value errors still propagate)
- All 36 tests pass, `oxlint` reports 0 errors, 0 warnings

**Terminal evidence (commit 0cf2718):**

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-config.test.ts src/acp/control-plane/runtime-options.test.ts
 ✓ ../../src/acp/control-plane/runtime-options.test.ts (15 tests) 5ms
 ✓ ../../src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-config.test.ts (21 tests) 27ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  36 passed (36)

$ pnpm exec oxlint src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-controls.ts src/acp/control-plane/runtime-options.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

**Live validation:** The same prevention-layer logic was applied as a compiled JS patch to a running OpenClaw instance targeting an OpenCode ACP backend. Before the patch, every ACP spawn failed with `ACP_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED_CONTROL`. After the patch, the thinking config option was silently skipped and session startup completed normally through a full first turn.
